**Checking the structure of the answer**

- **Closure:** If $H'$ is an induced subgraph of $H$, every induced $H$-subdivision contains an induced $H'$-subdivision, so $\mathcal{C}_{H'}\subseteq\mathcal{C}_H$. The property is therefore closed under induced subgraphs, as the problem states.
- **4-vertex graphs:** There are 11 graphs on 4 vertices. Each of the eight outside $\{P_4, \text{paw}, \text{diamond}\}$ is excluded by an unbounded-clique-width family. $K_{1,3}$, $C_4$, $2K_2$, $P_3\cup K_1$, $K_3\cup K_1$, $4K_1$, $K_2\cup 2K_1$ and $K_4$ are excluded by claw-free graphs, chordal/split graphs, complements of triangle-free graphs, complements of line graphs of walls, and line graphs of cubic graphs, as appropriate. The proposed killers are not all correctly justified, but the conclusions hold.
- **Sufficiency:** $\mathcal{C}_{P_4}$ is the class of $P_4$-free graphs (cographs), which has clique-width at most 2. The paw and diamond cases are plausible but not verified here. The diamond case reduces to theta-free graphs, which have block structure of cliques and cycles.
- **Larger graphs:** Gem has all 4-vertex induced subgraphs in the surviving list, so it is a real candidate. It is excluded by the wall argument, since walls have maximum degree 3 and gem has a vertex of degree 4. The kite is excluded via its induced $K_3\cup K_1$. I did not check every 5-vertex graph, so this step rests on the proposed argument.
- **Edge counts:** $P_4$ has 3 edges, the paw has 4, and the diamond has 5. The sum is $12$.

The conclusion that the maximal set is $\{P_4, \text{paw}, \text{diamond}\}$ is consistent with the 4-vertex analysis and with the wall-based exclusion of higher-degree and nonplanar graphs. I recall a result of this shape in the literature, but I could not verify it, and the sufficiency for the paw and diamond and the completeness over 5-vertex graphs are not fully checked. The arithmetic and the 4-vertex case analysis are solid.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
